rationale: A wins because it does the one thing this update needs: it treats the core claim as unproven, with "\"Minutes\" is a claim, not a capability, until something is in orbit." That is sharper strategic material than B's padded category wrapper, "The Race to Spot a Wildfire From Space Before It Becomes a Disaster," which invents a race because the facts only gave us one pre-launch startup. A still has factual sloppiness, but its proof demands and reporter targeting are more useful to a founder before they walk into interviews.
gaps_in_A: "no revenue" is not grounded. The update says revenue is not disclosed, which is very different from no revenue.
"agencies are signing before the hardware exists" turns one unnamed MOU into a plural trend. One agency is not a market pattern.
"before a lookout tower does" invents a comparison system the update never named.
The trend angle is doing cleanup in its own proof section: "at least two or three other companies" means the angle is not ready yet.
gaps_in_B: "The Race to Spot a Wildfire From Space" invents a competitive race. The update names no competitors, incumbents, or other entrants.
"June timing places this at the opening of Northern Hemisphere fire season" is a convenient peg, not a supplied fact; use it only with actual regional fire-season support.
"satellites that don't exist yet" overstates the record. We know none are in orbit, not that no hardware exists.
It refuses "Trend (commercial space for climate adaptation)" because one company is not a trend, then keeps a "category-creation" angle built on the same thin evidence. Pick a lane.
